concepts.title: Reflection of Light by Spherical Mirrors
concepts.definition: Reflection follows the rule that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection; spherical mirrors - concave converging and convex diverging - form images located by pole, centre of curvature, principal focus and focal length, with concave mirrors making real or virtual images and convex mirrors always making small virtual ones.
concepts.key_idea: Equal angles, mirror geometry: focus and pole map every image's position and nature.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc109.txt sections on reflection and spherical mirrors

concepts.title: Mirror Formula, Magnification and Refraction
concepts.definition: Object distance u, image distance v and focal length f connect through the mirror formula, and magnification m equals the image height over object height; light then bends on entering glass - refraction - governed by Snell's law, and lenses focus light with their own power in dioptres.
concepts.key_idea: One formula relates u, v and f; magnification scales the image height.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh109 mirror formula, magnification and refraction sections

solution_steps.action: divide the image height by the object height
solution_steps.explain: Magnification is the ratio of heights.

concepts.title: Power of a Lens and Image Formation by Lenses
concepts.definition: A convex lens converges and a concave lens diverges light; the lens formula connects object distance, image distance and focal length, and the power of a lens - the degree of convergence or divergence - equals the reciprocal of focal length in metres, measured in dioptres.
concepts.key_idea: Short focal length, strong lens: power is 1 over f in dioptres.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh109 sections on lenses, lens formula and power
